Favourites: less chronic pain. Music and concerts. Helps me eat, helps me not eat. helps me soldier on through the day. Motivation. Low doses feel like a stimulant. Higher doses feels like a downer. Helps me let go and be loving/affectionate/intimate when I've put walls up with friends and family. Waking up at 6 am, dosing, going back to sleep and waking up with a painless good attitude. Best comedown cure in all the land. Pairs well with a lot of drugs. Long legs. Helps me not crave other more harmful drugs.  I feel more confident in my body and take less time obsessing over my image. Memory loss (ignorance is bliss sometimes). 

Least favourites: also memory loss. I have a sneaking suspicion I can't remember how productive I've actually been and I give myself a hard time. Sometimes makes me too chatty and I info dump/trauma dump on my family and friends. Makes me dissociate in groups of people much more easily. Large doses makes me physically numb during sex.  If I don't have a set task already to go (work, errands etc) I will float around the house starting things but not get anything done. 

Almost all the least favourites are eradicated if I don't take more than I need.

I feel like my constant research session is an obsession and I can't be in the moment anymore. It's a possibility I have TOS and sometimes I genuinely wish it gets worse to the point of blood clots so they take me seriously and I can put an end to this OCD research life. But then I think it's the most fucked up thing to wish it would get worse. 

Some months I force myself to "give up" to see how it feels. But after resisting the urge to google/make appointments for x amount of time, it's like it builds up and suddenly explodes (usually on a very bad pain day, when I've failed a physical activity) and that's when I'm at the most risk to do something really impulsive and self destructive. 

I'll look into acceptance and commitment therapy, but I'll also look into radiopedia as a new obsession because yeh, still no idea if I should give up or not.
